title: Connected shippinTECH workspace: Google Drive and Microsoft 365 files

costar.context: The owner requests a usable shippinTECH app built around integration with Microsoft 365, Google Drive, Docs and extensible third-party components.
costar.objective: Deliver a working connection hub, shared file-provider interface, existing Google adapter and Microsoft Graph browser connector with documented setup and executable checks.
costar.style: Implement vertical user workflows with honest capability boundaries.
costar.audience: People testing the local app and future connector implementers.
costar.response: UI, connector modules, tests and local setup documentation.

concerns: Real Microsoft/Google consent requires app registration and a user account; tests against substitutes are not live-provider proof.
Microsoft browser tokens must remain in MSAL memory, be cleared on shippinTECH sign-out/account change, and never be sent to the mail server or arbitrary Graph pagination URLs.
Use explicit user gestures for sign-in and transfers. No background cross-provider copying or mail/calendar consent.
Provider download URLs are short-lived credentials; do not persist or log them.
Google backend remains coupled to the inherited engine. This integration slice does not complete the independent-engine rewrite.
MSAL may require a dedicated popup bridge page depending on installed version; inspect installed supported APIs.
The existing operating-tree checker has unrelated failing records.
context: Continue independent-product direction with tangible integration functionality instead of further replacement-only planning.
current_state: Google OAuth, browsing, exports and per-file copies exist. There is no Microsoft connector or common connection hub. Drive and Docs appear only in admin navigation. Svelte builds as static assets.
target_design: Provider-neutral TypeScript file interface and reusable Svelte browser, with Google using existing same-origin server endpoints and Microsoft using official MSAL plus delegated Graph access. The Microsoft connector uses public application configuration and a dedicated popup redirect, no client secret. File metadata normalizes IDs, folders, source URLs and export formats. Own Drive stays behind its existing adapter. Normal signed-in navigation exposes the workspace and connections for local testing.
changes: Add a provider contract and Google/Microsoft adapters with normalized metadata and capabilities.

Add Microsoft sign-in, memory-only session lifecycle, OneDrive list/search/pagination and file download using Graph-provided download URLs. Start with read-only consent; opening Office documents uses their existing Microsoft URLs.
Add a Connections route with provider state, sign-in/disconnect, folder navigation, search, export/download and copy into shippinTECH Drive; expose Drive/Docs/Connections in signed-in navigation.
Add transfer bounds, stale-response protection, explicit disconnect confirmation and provider-specific recovery messages.
Document public app configuration and connector extension points, with a tested-capability matrix and clear omissions.
Run typecheck, unit, build and mocked browser interaction/accessibility tests. Record real-provider proof as pending.
boundaries: No real account sign-in, external publication, release, customer mail or background data movement.
No credentials in chat, source, logs or URLs; Microsoft application ID is public configuration, not a secret.
No claim of Outlook/Gmail sync, SharePoint site discovery, embedded Office editing, continuous synchronization or completed engine independence.
Leave existing Google connection and files routes compatible; preserve unrelated untracked plan.

verification.name: ui-contracts
verification.proves: Types and existing/new UI behavior remain consistent.
verification.expected: No new errors; report baseline failures.

verification.name: workspace-browser
verification.proves: The assembled route can browse, search, handle failures, copy explicit files, disconnect and gate signed-out access with mocked provider responses.
verification.expected: Desktop/mobile tests and accessibility checks pass.

verification.name: static-build
verification.proves: Production-format static assets include the route and Microsoft auth callback without bundling server-only dependencies.
verification.expected: Build succeeds; this is a build check, not a production readiness claim.
